loo-2.configuration:
Model: Random-effects
Estimator: DerSimonian–Laird
Confidence level: 95%
Each omission row excludes the named study; compare with the all-studies estimate.
RR = 1 means equal risks in BCG vaccine and Control; estimates are fitted on the log scale.
Inference: Normal approximation
loo-2.results: In total, 13 studies were included (191,064 participants in BCG vaccine, 166,283 in Control). With all studies, the pooled risk ratio was 0.49 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.70; I² = 92.12%). Across all 13 omission fits, pooled estimates ranged from 0.45 (omitting TB Prevention Trial, 1980) to 0.54 (omitting Hart & Sutherland, 1977). I² after omission ranged from 83.82% (omitting TB Prevention Trial, 1980) to 92.77% (omitting Coetzee & Berjak, 1968). Table 1 gives every omission fit.

factor-2.configuration:
Model: Random-effects meta-regression
Estimator: Restricted maximum likelihood (REML)
Confidence level: 95%
Moderators: Subgroup
Bubble size increases with model weight; sizes are rescaled for legibility and do not show exact relative weights.
OR = 1 means equal odds in Aspirin and Control; estimates are fitted on the log scale.
Inference: Normal approximation
factor-2.results: In total, 6 studies were included (5,599 participants in Aspirin, 5,217 in Control); 1 study was excluded. For Subgroup: Later trials vs Earlier trials (reference), the coefficient was 0.28 (95% CI −0.03 to 0.58; z = 1.79; P = 0.074). Residual heterogeneity: Q = 4.25 (df = 4; P = 0.373); I² = 22.15%; τ² = 0.01. In Earlier trials (reference), the pooled odds ratio was 0.75 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.93). In Later trials, the pooled odds ratio was 0.98 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.21).
